BiblicalUsage: Chala means to be sick, and it appears once, of Asa: in the thirty-ninth year of his reign he was diseased in his feet until his disease was exceeding great, yet in his disease he sought not the LORD, but the physicians.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Asa's sickness is the warning that the cure matters less than the turning: he sought the physicians and not the LORD.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
